questions.question: Which operating system is associated with the classic Cisco 2811 ISR?
questions.explanation: The 2811 belongs to the classic ISR generation running Cisco IOS.

option_explanations.A: The 2811 belongs to the classic ISR generation running Cisco IOS.
option_explanations.B: IOS XR targets carrier routing platforms.
option_explanations.C: NX-OS is associated with Nexus data-center switches.
option_explanations.D: CatOS was a legacy Catalyst switching OS.

questions.question: Which family runs on a Catalyst 9300?
questions.explanation: Catalyst 9300 switches use IOS XE, which retains an IOS-style CLI.

option_explanations.A: Catalyst 9300 switches use IOS XE, which retains an IOS-style CLI.
option_explanations.B: IOS XR is used on carrier platforms such as ASR 9000.
option_explanations.C: NX-OS is used on Nexus switches.

questions.question: Which OS would you expect on a Nexus 9000 running in standalone NX-OS mode?

option_explanations.A: Legacy CatOS is not the Nexus standalone OS.
option_explanations.B: IOS XR is for carrier routing platforms.
option_explanations.C: Classic IOS is a different software family from NX-OS.

questions.question: The inventory shows an ASR 9000 running IOS XR. A technician downloaded an IOS XE image for an ASR 1000. Which action is appropriate before upgrading?

options.A: Obtain an IOS XR image supported for the exact ASR 9000 model
options.B: Use a Nexus image because the router is a modular platform
options.C: Use the IOS XE image because both routers carry the ASR name
options.D: Rename the IOS XE image to match the current boot image

questions.explanation: The recorded operating system and hardware determine image compatibility across the two product lines.

option_explanations.A: The recorded operating system and hardware determine image compatibility across the two product lines.
option_explanations.B: A Nexus image targets Nexus hardware.
option_explanations.C: ASR 1000 and ASR 9000 use different software families.
option_explanations.D: Renaming an image cannot make its binaries compatible.

questions.question: An archival Catalyst configuration uses commands such as set vlan. Which legacy operating system does this suggest?
questions.explanation: The set-based syntax is characteristic of CatOS on older Catalyst switches.

option_explanations.A: NX-OS is not the legacy Catalyst set-command environment.
option_explanations.B: IOS XR uses a different configuration syntax and commit model.
option_explanations.C: The set-based syntax is characteristic of CatOS on older Catalyst switches.
option_explanations.D: IOS XE uses IOS-style configuration, such as vlan in global configuration mode.

questions.question: What architectural description fits IOS XE?

options.A: CatOS runs inside an IOS XR process
options.B: The device boots directly into a single CatOS executable
options.C: IOS control-plane functionality runs as a process on a Linux-based system
options.D: NX-OS supplies the only configuration interface

questions.explanation: IOS XE runs IOSd on a Linux-based architecture while retaining familiar IOS commands.

option_explanations.A: IOS XE does not embed legacy CatOS inside IOS XR.
option_explanations.B: CatOS is a separate legacy operating system.
option_explanations.C: IOS XE runs IOSd on a Linux-based architecture while retaining familiar IOS commands.
option_explanations.D: NX-OS is a distinct OS and does not supply the IOS XE CLI.

questions.question: On IOS XR, an engineer sees a pending interface description in the candidate configuration. A second session sees the old description in the running configuration. Which action should the engineer take?

options.A: Review and commit the candidate change
options.B: Apply the equivalent NX-OS interface command
options.C: Copy the running configuration to a remote backup
options.D: Exit from the second session and reopen it

questions.explanation: IOS XR applies the contents of the candidate configuration to running state at commit.

option_explanations.A: IOS XR applies the contents of the candidate configuration to running state at commit.
option_explanations.B: NX-OS commands do not apply a pending IOS XR candidate change.
option_explanations.C: A backup captures the current state without committing the candidate.
option_explanations.D: Reopening the second session still shows the unchanged running configuration.

questions.question: Two devices are branded ASR. What evidence should you use to choose their software command references?

options.C: The exact hardware model and installed software release

questions.explanation: Cisco uses the ASR name across distinct platforms that can run different operating systems.

option_explanations.A: The ASR brand spans hardware families and software trains.
option_explanations.B: The cable determines console connectivity, not the installed CLI.
option_explanations.C: Cisco uses the ASR name across distinct platforms that can run different operating systems.
option_explanations.D: Subnet size has no bearing on the platform's command syntax.

questions.question: Which command would you use first on an unfamiliar Cisco CLI to identify the software release for documentation lookup?
questions.explanation: The version display identifies installed software and typically includes platform information.

option_explanations.A: The routing table describes destinations and next hops.
option_explanations.B: Interface output describes ports and link state.
option_explanations.C: The version display identifies installed software and typically includes platform information.
option_explanations.D: The ARP table maps IPv4 neighbors to link-layer addresses.

questions.question: An older Catalyst chassis used CatOS for switching and a separate IOS routing module. What should an engineer do before migrating it to an IOS XE campus switch?

options.A: Load the routing module image as the switch startup configuration
options.B: Translate the switching and routing settings to the target CLI
options.C: Copy the CatOS configuration verbatim into IOS XE
options.D: Convert every set command into an IOS XR commit

questions.explanation: The separate legacy configuration contexts and CatOS syntax must be translated and reviewed for the new platform.

option_explanations.A: A routing module image is executable software, not a configuration file.
option_explanations.B: The separate legacy configuration contexts and CatOS syntax must be translated and reviewed for the new platform.
option_explanations.C: CatOS switch commands differ from IOS XE syntax.
option_explanations.D: IOS XR commits do not translate settings for an IOS XE target.
